papers.title: On the estimation and validity of AI time horizons---a statistical look at the METR plot
papers.abstract: METR's 50\% time horizon measures the human completion time of software tasks that an AI solves with 50\% probability, allowing AI capabilities to be expressed in interpretable units. On 228 tasks and 26 AIs, we recompute the time horizons using splines and item-response theory to relax the assumption that the AI difficulty of a task depends linearly on the log of human time. Our fitted spline can be interpreted as a function that \emph{converts} human time to AI difficulty; it is nearly flat in a region from 2--30 min but close to linear elsewhere. Hence, a time-horizon jump from 3 min to 30 min is much easier than one from 30 min to 5 hours despite the same multiplier of $10 \times$. Overall, we contribute time-horizon point estimates that perform better under a cross-validated suite of proper scoring rules, as well as diagnostic plots for assessing time horizons' construct validity. We suggest that time horizons be interpreted together with the diagnostic plots, especially as new time-horizon-based benchmarks are proposed or existing ones grow to include longer tasks.
papers.summary_zh: METR的50%时间跨度用人类完成时间衡量AI能力，但假设任务AI难度与人类时间对数线性相关。本文用样条和项目反应理论在228个任务、26个AI上重新计算时间跨度，拟合样条可视为人类时间到AI难度的转换函数。新估计在交叉验证评分规则下更优，且样条在2-30分钟近乎平坦，表明3分钟到30分钟的跨度跳跃远易于30分钟到5小时，建议结合诊断图解释时间跨度。
papers.summary_en: METR's 50% time horizon measures AI capability in human-time units but assumes AI difficulty is linear in log human time. We recompute time horizons on 228 tasks and 26 AIs using splines and item-response theory, yielding a spline that converts human time to AI difficulty. Our estimates perform better under cross-validated proper scoring rules, and the spline is nearly flat from 2-30 min, implying a 3-to-30 min jump is much easier than 30 min to 5 hours; we recommend interpreting time horizons with diagnostic plots.
highlights_zh: 用样条+IRT放松线性假设
交叉验证下评分规则更优
需结合诊断图评估构念效度

papers.title: From Reactive Containment to Proactive Assurance: Lessons from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Agent Security Incidents
papers.abstract: In 2026, cybersecurity evaluations involving OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google agents reached real systems outside their authorized test scope. The paths were different. OpenAI agents exploited research infrastructure, coordinated across runs, and compromised parts of Hugging Face's production environment. Anthropic reported cases in which a misconfigured third-party environment exposed real systems to agents pursuing simulated cyber tasks. In a separately reported evaluation, Google's Gemini accessed three real organizations through an unintended internet route; Google stated that the model stopped in all three instances. Taken together, the cases show why an evaluation cannot rely on an assumed boundary. That boundary must be verified while the agent is operating. This comparative instrumental case study develops a Proactive Agent Security Assurance Cycle (PASAC) and a five-layer Boundary Assurance Stack. The framework combines risk-tiered task design, executable scope contracts, pre-run validation, least-capability access, independent egress enforcement, credential restrictions, cross-run monitoring, automatic stop conditions, and evidence-based reauthorization. A leading-indicator model, nine design propositions, and seven falsifiable hypotheses turn these lessons into a testable research program. Because the public Gemini record is limited to attributed statements and journalism, its detailed causal mechanism remains provisional. The central conclusion is straightforward: proactive agent security requires continuous assurance across the full execution system, not confidence in any single sandbox or safeguard.
papers.summary_zh: 2026年OpenAI、Anthropic和Google的智能体安全评估突破授权测试边界，触及真实系统，暴露出依赖假定边界的安全评估不可靠。该研究通过比较性工具性案例研究提出主动式智能体安全保障周期（PASAC）与五层边界保障栈，整合风险分级任务设计、可执行范围契约、运行前验证、最小能力访问、独立出口管控、跨运行监控与自动停止条件。研究给出领先指标模型、九项设计命题和七项可证伪假设，将教训转化为可测试研究议程，核心结论是主动式智能体安全需要覆盖整个执行系统的持续保障。
papers.summary_en: In 2026, cybersecurity evaluations of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google agents reached real systems beyond authorized test scopes, showing that evaluations cannot rely on assumed boundaries. This comparative instrumental case study develops a Proactive Agent Security Assurance Cycle (PASAC) and a five-layer Boundary Assurance Stack, combining risk-tiered task design, executable scope contracts, pre-run validation, least-capability access, independent egress enforcement, credential restrictions, cross-run monitoring, automatic stop conditions, and evidence-based reauthorization. It contributes a leading-indicator model, nine design propositions, and seven falsifiable hypotheses, concluding that proactive agent security requires continuous assurance across the full execution system rather than confidence in any single sandbox or safeguard.
highlights_zh: 提出PASAC与五层边界保障栈
构建九命题七假设可测试框架
需持续保障而非单点沙箱信任

papers.title: CSF: Contextual Safety Filtering for Motion Generators
papers.abstract: Text-conditioned motion generators produce trackable whole-body motion, but they have no notion of scene-dependent safety: the same action may target an object or a person. Existing safeguards either inspect the prompt, require labeled motion data, or enforce geometric constraints; therefore, they do not directly account for how scene context changes a motion's meaning. We introduce contextual safety filtering (CSF), a training-free filter that grounds natural-language safety rules in safe and unsafe reference trajectories produced by the generator. For each active rule, safe and unsafe reference trajectories define an affine safety value that a safe reference tracking CBF-QP enforces. Across four pretrained generators with different architectures, CSF activates the intended rules in all explicit and scene-triggered unsafe cases and reduces the danger-event rate by up to 90%, while preserving 88-100% of benign motions. We demonstrate the complete system on a real-world Unitree G1, where it successfully prevents unsafe motions in a variety of scenarios, including interactions with humans and objects.

papers.title: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control
papers.abstract: General-purpose robots must perform a wide range of tasks from agile locomotion to dexterous manipulation. While sim-to-real reinforcement learning (RL) has proven to be a useful tool for this goal, current RL pipelines depend on engineering-heavy, per-task structural priors such as shaped rewards and demonstrations. Recent work has shown that diverse simulator resets, combined with massively parallel simulation, can alleviate much of this engineering burden on several manipulation problems. However, we find that naively scaling this paradigm to more precise or dynamic problems remains non-trivial. While simulator resets can help with exploration, uniformly sampling over this distribution wastes a growing fraction of learning experience on task configurations the policy has already mastered or cannot yet attempt. This makes it challenging to see the expected benefits of scaling parallel environments for RL, since much of the learning signal in a batch is wasted during learning. To mitigate this, we introduce Success Guided Sampling (SGS), a simple adaptive sampler that concentrates RL training on task configurations around the frontier of the policy's capabilities. Doing so allows large-scale simulated RL to make the most out of the experience in a batch, enabling much more effective scaling to large-scale parallel simulation. Across experiments using up to $2^{20}$ (over one million) parallel environments, SGS enables RL to solve challenging multi-terrain quadruped locomotion and contact-rich assembly tasks that prior methods fail to solve. Finally, we distill the learned manipulation policies into RGB-based policies and demonstrate zero-shot transfer to several challenging assembly tasks on real hardware. Project website: https://sgs-rl.github.io/.

papers.title: FastBench: Can Streaming VLMs Perceive High-Dynamic Real-World Streams?
papers.abstract: Streaming Video Large Language Models (VLMs) enable continuous video understanding, yet existing benchmarks focus on low-dynamic scenarios. Under bounded context budgets, models must balance temporal history, spatial resolution, and temporal granularity; sparse sampling at 1--2 FPS misses fast events. We introduce FastBench to evaluate high-dynamic perception in real-world video streams. Its trajectory-grounded pipeline combines QA generation from high-FPS clips, filtering of questions answerable at 2 FPS, answer verification using SAM3 and CoTracker3 trajectories, and three rounds of human inspection. FastBench contains 306 QA pairs across eight domains, six capabilities, and forward, instant, and backward temporal scopes, with human-annotated evidence intervals. We also present ProactiveFrame, a training-free baseline that adjusts incoming frame rates through text tokens. A dual-tier sliding window retains recent high-FPS observations while downsampling older ones into sparse history. Experiments reveal substantial limitations: the strongest model, Gemini-3.5-Flash, scores only 50.7%. Denser sampling improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 32.9% at 2 FPS to 44.6% at 24 FPS, but gains saturate as history is compressed. ProactiveFrame outperforms sparse uniform sampling by 5.4 and 1.5 percentage points, yet remains well below oracle-guided focusing, showing that current VLMs struggle to determine from the stream alone when finer temporal perception is needed. FastBench provides a testbed for high-dynamic streaming video understanding. Code and data: https://github.com/Ashone3/FastBench.
papers.summary_zh: 现有流式视频大模型基准多聚焦低动态场景，在有限上下文预算下难以捕捉高速事件。本文提出FastBench，基于轨迹生成高动态视频问答并过滤2FPS可答问题，同时提出免训练基线ProactiveFrame，通过文本令牌自适应调整帧率并采用双层滑窗保留近期高帧率观测。实验显示最强模型仅得50.7%，密集采样收益随历史压缩而饱和，表明当前VLM难以自主判断何时需要更细粒度的时间感知。
papers.summary_en: Existing streaming video LLM benchmarks focus on low-dynamic scenarios, where bounded context budgets force a trade-off among temporal history, spatial resolution, and temporal granularity, causing sparse 1-2 FPS sampling to miss fast events. We introduce FastBench, a trajectory-grounded pipeline that generates QA from high-FPS clips, filters out questions answerable at 2 FPS, verifies answers with SAM3 and CoTracker3 trajectories, and includes three rounds of human inspection, plus ProactiveFrame, a training-free baseline that adapts incoming frame rates via text tokens and uses a dual-tier sliding window. Experiments show the best model, Gemini-3.5-Flash, reaches only 50.7%, denser sampling improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 32.9% to 44.6% but saturates, and ProactiveFrame beats sparse uniform sampling by 5.4 and 1.5 points yet lags oracle-guided focusing, revealing that current VLMs struggle to decide when finer temporal perception is needed.
highlights_zh: 轨迹校验的高动态流式视频基准
最强模型仅达50.7%准确率
揭示VLM难以自主判断采样需求

papers.title: WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) struggle with spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal reasoning. We hypothesize that these failures reflect a shared deficit in visual transition reasoning, and test whether this capability can serve as a shared training primitive, one that different models can learn from different supervision sources and reuse across different tasks, with a systematic training recipe. Existing benchmarks document these deficits separately but do not support controlled comparisons across scenes, actions, and reasoning operations. We therefore introduce WOVEN, a training source and benchmark for visual transition reasoning that organizes transition supervision by scene, action, and reasoning type, using diverse, realistic rollouts from video-pretrained generative models: 36,076 examples across 20 scene types, 5 action types, and 8 reasoning types. We first evaluate 38 frontier MLLMs (e.g., GPT-5.4 and Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B) and find a substantial and systematic deficit: even the strongest models fall far below humans, and the failures recur across model families and persist with scale. We then train MLLMs at multiple scales on WOVEN and find that they learn a shared capability that transfers broadly: training subsets of only about 2,000 items each collectively improve 22 of 26 external benchmarks by up to 27.3 percentage points, and WOVEN data can replace 30-50% of a task's own training data with comparable accuracy. Controlled comparisons further yield a training recipe for visual world modeling, validated prospectively on held-out benchmarks: select supervision by the reasoning operation it teaches rather than by the actions, scenes, or domains it shows, and prefer larger changes to the visual state for robustness. Our work establishes visual transition reasoning as a reusable foundation for systematic visual world-model training in MLLMs.
papers.summary_zh: 多模态大模型在空间、具身、物理和时间推理上表现不佳，作者假设这些失败源于共同的视觉转移推理能力缺陷。为此提出WOVEN，一个按场景、动作和推理类型组织的视觉转移推理训练源与基准，包含来自视频预训练生成模型的36,076个多样化真实rollout样本，并系统评测了38个前沿MLLM。结果显示这些模型存在系统性缺陷，而用WOVEN训练可学到可迁移的共享能力，仅约2,000样本的子集即可在26个外部基准中的22个上提升最多27.3个百分点，并可替代30-50%的任务自有训练数据，确立了视觉转移推理作为MLLM视觉世界模型训练的可复用基础。
papers.summary_en: Multimodal LLMs struggle with spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal reasoning, which the authors hypothesize stems from a shared deficit in visual transition reasoning. They introduce WOVEN, a training source and benchmark organizing transition supervision by scene, action, and reasoning type with 36,076 realistic rollouts from video-pretrained generative models, and evaluate 38 frontier MLLMs. They find a systematic deficit across models, but show that training on WOVEN yields a transferable shared capability: subsets of ~2,000 items improve 22 of 26 external benchmarks by up to 27.3 points and can replace 30-50% of task-specific data, establishing visual transition reasoning as a reusable foundation for visual world-model training in MLLMs.
highlights_zh: 按推理类型组织监督的视觉转移训练源
2千样本提升22/26基准最多27.3点
可替代30-50%任务数据，跨模型迁移
highlights_en: Transition supervision organized by reasoning type
2K samples boost 22/26 benchmarks up to 27.3 pts
Replaces 30-50% task data, transfers across models

papers.title: Dex-One2Many: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from a Single Human Demonstration
papers.abstract: While learning dexterous manipulation from a single human video offers a promising alternative to costly robot demonstrations, many recent methods predominantly imitate demonstrated motions. Such strict motion matching often limits generalization to initial object poses, goal poses, and grasps not shown in the video. Alternatively, discovering a policy via reinforcement learning (RL) allows for broad generalization, but without prior guidance, it struggles with high-dimensional exploration in complex, multi-stage tasks. To address these coupled generalization and exploration challenges, we present Dex-One2Many, a real-to-sim-to-real framework that learns a generalizable dexterous manipulation policy from a single human video. Our key insight is to abstract the video into sequential scene graphs that guide RL, enabling efficient exploration while preserving broad generalizability. The graphs serve as generative constraints for sampling diverse reset states and provide dense rewards for each stage. Because the graphs constrain relations rather than exact poses, these reset states cover object poses and grasps beyond the video, while initializing each stage from them with dense rewards keeps exploration short and guided. Trained entirely in simulation, Dex-One2Many transfers zero-shot to a real multi-fingered hand. Across five tool-use and manipulation tasks, Dex-One2Many exceeds baselines by 6.5% in seen configurations, while its robust generalization widens this gap to 71% in unseen scenarios.
papers.summary_zh: 从单个人类视频学习灵巧操作时，现有方法多严格模仿动作，难以泛化到新初始位姿、目标位姿和抓取方式，而强化学习虽泛化性强却面临高维探索困难。为此，作者提出Dex-One2Many，将视频抽象为序列化场景图来引导强化学习，生成多样化重置状态并提供分阶段密集奖励，从而在保持泛化性的同时实现高效探索。该方法完全在仿真中训练，可零样本迁移到真实多指手，在五项任务中已见配置超越基线6.5%，未见场景下优势扩大至71%。
papers.summary_en: Learning dexterous manipulation from a single human video often suffers from strict motion imitation, limiting generalization to novel object poses, goals, and grasps, while reinforcement learning generalizes broadly but struggles with high-dimensional exploration. Dex-One2Many addresses this by abstracting the video into sequential scene graphs that guide RL, generating diverse reset states and dense per-stage rewards to enable efficient yet generalizable exploration. Trained purely in simulation and transferred zero-shot to a real multi-fingered hand, it outperforms baselines by 6.5% on seen configurations and by 71% in unseen scenarios across five tool-use and manipulation tasks.
highlights_zh: 用序列场景图引导RL，兼顾泛化与探索
未见场景下性能领先基线71%
仿真训练零样本迁移真实多指手

papers.title: Rubric-CEPR: Self-Evolving Image Editing via Reward-Verified Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Instruction-guided image editors have become highly capable, yet improving them further still depends on human-edited training pairs or external reward models. Such supervision is costly to obtain and can reward plausible failures: a realistic output may leave the requested change undone or alter content that should be preserved. In this work, we strive to improve a pretrained image editor using only its own generations, without human-edited targets or an external training-time reward model. To this end, we propose a self-evolving framework, named Rubric-CEPR, that verifies the editor's own samples with its internal representations through a rubric-augmented Contrastive Edit-Preservation Reward (CEPR). A Planner proposes structured edit instructions from unlabeled images, the Editor samples multiple candidate edits, and a frozen Critic scores each candidate with decomposed rubric checks for edit realization, removal of the old state, and content preservation, using features already exposed by the editor. Non-compensatory gates reject infeasible candidates, and the best verified candidate is distilled into the editor through lightweight adapter training. On Qwen-Image-Edit, Rubric-CEPR improves ImgEdit from 4.36 to 4.60 (+5.5%), with a +24.9% gain on object isolation, and transfers to GEdit-Bench and Complex-Edit. The same procedure also improves Step1X-Edit by +7.8% on ImgEdit. We hope our approach will serve as a solid baseline for image editors that improve themselves from their own verified samples. Our code is publicly available at $\href{https://riteshthawkar.github.io/Rubric-CEPR/}{\text{this URL}}$
papers.summary_zh: 指令引导的图像编辑器性能提升通常依赖人工编辑的训练对或外部奖励模型，这类监督成本高且可能奖励看似合理但未完成编辑或破坏保留内容的失败样本。本文提出Rubric-CEPR自进化框架，利用编辑器自身内部表示，通过评分标准增强的对比编辑-保留奖励（CEPR）验证自生成样本，经规划器提出指令、编辑器采样候选、冻结评论家按分解评分标准打分，并用非补偿门控筛选后蒸馏最佳候选到轻量适配器中。在Qwen-Image-Edit上，ImgEdit从4.36提升至4.60（+5.5%），物体隔离任务提升24.9%，并迁移至GEdit-Bench和Complex-Edit，Step1X-Edit也提升7.8%，为无需人工目标或外部奖励的自提升图像编辑器提供了可靠基线。
papers.summary_en: Improving instruction-guided image editors typically relies on human-edited training pairs or external reward models, which are costly and can reward plausible failures that leave edits undone or alter preserved content. This work proposes Rubric-CEPR, a self-evolving framework that verifies the editor's own samples using its internal representations via a rubric-augmented Contrastive Edit-Preservation Reward (CEPR), where a Planner proposes instructions, the Editor samples candidates, and a frozen Critic scores them with decomposed rubric checks, followed by non-compensatory gating and distillation into lightweight adapters. On Qwen-Image-Edit, Rubric-CEPR improves ImgEdit from 4.36 to 4.60 (+5.5%) with a +24.9% gain on object isolation, transfers to GEdit-Bench and Complex-Edit, and also improves Step1X-Edit by +7.8%, offering a solid baseline for self-improving image editors from their own verified samples.
highlights_zh: 内部表示验证的自进化编辑框架
无需人工目标或外部奖励模型

papers.title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
papers.abstract: We propose BrickBench, a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design. Given a prompt, an agent is tasked with producing an assembly that not only satisfies semantic and design criteria, but that can also be physically built. To do so, it must select parts from a discrete library and reason jointly about local and global constraints. We score validity, alignment, and design across three settings that vary in scale and part availability. We provide BrickAgent, an environment for coding agents to construct, inspect, and validate their designs. We find that leading agents largely satisfy verifiable physical and semantic requirements, but fall short of human designs. We release our benchmark and environment at http://www.brickben.ch
papers.summary_zh: 现有智能体在文本驱动的乐高套装设计上缺乏可同时评估语义、设计与可物理拼装性的基准。作者提出BrickBench基准与BrickAgent环境，让编码智能体从离散零件库中选件并联合推理局部与全局约束，在三种规模与零件可用性设置下评分有效性、对齐度与设计质量。结果显示领先智能体基本满足可验证的物理与语义要求，但仍逊于人类设计，为可建造性智能体设计研究提供了公开基准与工具。
papers.summary_en: Existing agents lack a benchmark for text-conditioned LEGO-set design that jointly evaluates semantics, design quality, and physical buildability. The authors introduce BrickBench and BrickAgent, an environment where coding agents select parts from a discrete library and reason about local and global constraints, scoring validity, alignment, and design across three settings of varying scale and part availability. Leading agents largely satisfy verifiable physical and semantic requirements but still fall short of human designs, offering a public benchmark and environment for buildable agentic design research.
highlights_zh: 提出可建造性乐高设计基准与环境
领先智能体达标但不及人类设计
推动可物理拼装的智能体设计研究

papers.title: Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems
papers.abstract: Bifurcations are ubiquitous in physical systems, from structural buckling to fluid and climate dynamics, yet they remain largely unexplored in deep learning. At a symmetry-breaking bifurcation, a single input admits multiple equally valid solutions, violating the one-to-one assumption underlying most learned physical surrogates. We introduce Bi-FORK, a generative framework for learning these one-to-many solution maps in high-dimensional systems. Bi-FORK generates complete trajectories through latent flow matching, preserving space and time coherence, and uses repulsion-guided sampling to recover distinct solution branches in a single amortized pass. We evaluate Bi-FORK on buckling beams, mechanical metamaterials, and Allen-Cahn phase separation, spanning continuous, discrete, and field-valued bifurcations with discretizations up to 260,000 points. Bi-FORK recovers the multimodal solution structure while scaling several orders of magnitude beyond prior approaches, opening generative modeling to high-dimensional bifurcating physical systems.
papers.summary_zh: 物理系统中的分岔（如结构屈曲、流体与气候动力学）普遍存在，但深度学习领域尚未充分探索；在对称破缺分岔处，单一输入对应多个有效解，违背了多数学习型物理代理模型的一对一假设。Bi-FORK 通过潜空间流匹配生成完整轨迹以保持时空连贯性，并利用排斥引导采样在单次摊销推理中恢复不同解分支。该方法在屈曲梁、机械超材料和 Allen-Cahn 相分离上验证，覆盖连续、离散和场值分岔，离散点数达 26 万，成功恢复多模态解结构并将规模扩展至先前方法的数个数量级，为高维分岔物理系统的生成建模开辟了新途径。
papers.summary_en: Bifurcations are ubiquitous in physical systems such as structural buckling and fluid/climate dynamics, yet they remain largely unexplored in deep learning; at symmetry-breaking bifurcations, a single input admits multiple valid solutions, violating the one-to-one assumption of most learned physical surrogates. Bi-FORK is a generative framework that learns these one-to-many solution maps by generating complete trajectories via latent flow matching to preserve space-time coherence and using repulsion-guided sampling to recover distinct solution branches in a single amortized pass. Evaluated on buckling beams, mechanical metamaterials, and Allen-Cahn phase separation across continuous, discrete, and field-valued bifurcations with up to 260,000 discretization points, Bi-FORK recovers multimodal solution structure while scaling several orders of magnitude beyond prior approaches, opening generative modeling to high-dimensional bifurcating physical systems.
highlights_zh: 潜空间流匹配+排斥引导采样
26万点离散化下恢复多解分支
高维分岔代理建模，尚属初步探索
